title: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS)
description: Enacted by Parliament (Act No. 45 of 2023). Replaced the Indian Penal Code (1860). Governs criminal offenses, public order, bodily safety, cyber crimes, mob lynching penalties, and community service sanctions across India.
ministry: Ministry of Home Affairs / Ministry of Law and Justice
longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the provisions relating to offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

amendmentHistory.title: Enactment & Presidential Assent
amendmentHistory.details: Passed by Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha; received Presidential assent on Dec 25, 2023.

amendmentHistory.title: Enforcement Notification
amendmentHistory.details: Brought into full statutory operation across India replacing IPC 1860.

sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.content:
(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
(2) It extends to the whole of India.
(3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

subsections.text: This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
It extends to the whole of India.

sections.title: Definitions

subsections.text: 'child' means any person below the age of eighteen years;

sections.title: Punishment for Murder
sections.content:
(1) Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
(2) When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

subsections.text: Punishment with death or imprisonment for life, and fine.
Mob lynching offense by group of 5 or more persons.

ministry: Ministry of Home Affairs
longTitle: An Act to provide a general Penal Code for India.

chapters.title: Of Offences Affecting the Human Body

sections.title: Punishment for Murder
sections.content: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.title: Dowry death
sections.content: (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death'.

title: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO)
description: Act No. 32 of 2012. Special statutory law to protect children below 18 years from sexual assault, harassment, and child pornography, establishing Special Courts and child-friendly trial procedures.

title: The Arms Act, 1959
description: Act No. 54 of 1959. Consolidates law relating to arms and ammunition to curb illegal weapons possession and manufacturing.

title: The Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002 (POTA)
description: Act No. 15 of 2002. Anti-terrorism legislation enacted to strengthen counter-terrorism enforcement mechanisms.

title: The Information Technology Act, 2000 (IT Act)
description: Act No. 21 of 2000. Provides legal recognition for transactions carried out by electronic data interchange, cyber offenses, digital signatures, electronic contracts, and intermediary liabilities.
ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
longTitle: An Act to provide legal recognition for transactions carried out by means of electronic data interchange and other means of electronic communication.
sourceAuthority: India Code / MeitY, Govt. of India

sections.title: Computer related offences
sections.content: If any person dishonestly or fraudulently does any act referred to in section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine.

sections.title: Punishment for violation of privacy
sections.content: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without consent shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years.

sections.title: Exemption from liability of intermediary in certain cases
sections.content: An intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by him if he observes due diligence.

title: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
description: Act No. 25 of 1955. Codifies laws relating to marriage, restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, void marriages, and divorce among Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs.

title: The Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939
description: Act No. 8 of 1939. Consolidates and clarifies provisions of Muslim law relating to suits for dissolution of marriage by women married under Muslim law.

title: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
description: Act No. 43 of 1954. Provides a special form of marriage for the people of India and all Indian nationals in foreign countries, irrespective of the religion or faith followed by either party.

title: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956
description: Act No. 30 of 1956. Amends and codifies the law relating to intestate succession among Hindus, giving equal coparcenary rights to daughters.

title: The Hindu Adoption & Maintenance Act, 1956
description: Act No. 78 of 1956. Codifies laws relating to adoption of children and statutory maintenance obligations towards wives, children, and aged parents.

title: The Guardians & Wards Act, 1890
description: Act No. 8 of 1890. Consolidates law relating to guardian and ward, welfare of minors, and custody proceedings.

title: The Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872
description: Act No. 15 of 1872. Consolidates law relating to solemnization of marriages of Christians in India.

title: The Parsi Marriage & Divorce Act, 1936
description: Act No. 3 of 1936. Governs marriage and divorce procedures among Parsi Zoroastrians.

title: The Divorce Act, 1869
description: Act No. 4 of 1869. Amends law relating to divorce and matrimonial causes for persons professing the Christian religion.

title: The Trade Union Act, 1926
description: Act No. 16 of 1926. Provides for the registration of Trade Unions and defines the law relating to registered Trade Unions.

title: The Factories Act, 1948
description: Act No. 63 of 1948. Regulates health, safety, welfare, working hours, and employment of workers in factories.

title: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
description: Act No. 14 of 1947. Regulates industrial relations, investigation and settlement of industrial disputes, strikes, lockouts, retrenchment, and lay-off compensation.

title: The Employee's Compensation Act, 1923
description: Act No. 8 of 1923. Provides payment of compensation to workmen for injury by accident sustained during employment.

title: The Minimum Wages Act, 1948
description: Act No. 11 of 1948. Provides for fixing minimum rates of wages in certain employments.

title: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
description: Act No. 4 of 1936. Regulates the payment of wages to certain classes of employed persons without unauthorized deductions.

title: The Environment Protection Act, 1986
description: Act No. 29 of 1986. Umbrella legislation designed to provide a framework for Central Government coordination of activities of various authorities under environmental laws.

title: The Air (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
description: Act No. 14 of 1981. Provides for the prevention, control, and abatement of air pollution in India.

title: The Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
description: Act No. 6 of 1974. Provides for the prevention and control of water pollution and maintaining water wholesomeness.

title: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
description: Act No. 53 of 1972. Provides protection to wild animals, birds, and plants to ensure ecological security.

title: The Advocates Act, 1961
description: Act No. 25 of 1961. Amends and consolidates law relating to legal practitioners and provides for the constitution of Bar Councils.

title: Bar Council of India Rules, 1975
description: Statutory rules framed under Advocates Act 1961 governing professional conduct, legal education, and disciplinary proceedings.

title: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC)
description: Act No. 5 of 1908. Fundamental code governing jurisdiction, trial procedure, pleadings, injunctions, execution of decrees, and civil appeals in Indian civil courts.
ministry: Ministry of Law and Justice
longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to the Procedure of the Courts of Civil Judicature.
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

sections.title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred
sections.content: The Courts shall (subject to the provisions herein contained) have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred.

sections.title: Res Judicata
sections.content: No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties...

sections.title: Settlement of disputes outside the Court (ADR)
sections.content: Where it appears to the Court that there exist elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, the Court shall formulate the terms of settlement and refer the same for Arbitration, Conciliation, Judicial Settlement or Mediation.

title: The Constitution of India, 1950
description: The supreme law of India. Contains 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 12 Schedules establishing fundamental rights, state policy, parliament, judiciary, and emergency powers.
ministry: Ministry of Law and Justice
longTitle: The supreme law of the Republic of India establishing fundamental rights, directive principles, and government frameworks.
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

sections.title: Equality before law
sections.content: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

sections.title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
sections.content: (1) All citizens shall have the right— (a) to freedom of speech and expression; (b) to assemble peaceably and without arms; (c) to form associations or unions; (d) to move freely throughout the territory of India...

sections.title: Protection of life and personal liberty
sections.content: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

sections.title: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by Part III (Writ Jurisdiction)
sections.content: (1) The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed. (2) The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari...

sections.title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
sections.content: Notwithstanding anything in Article 32 every High Court shall have powers, throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, to issue to any person or authority directions, orders or writs...

title: Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI)
description: Act No. 22 of 2005. Empowers citizens to request official information from public authorities, setting up Information Commissions.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
description: Act No. 35 of 2019. Established Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), e-commerce rules, product liability, and Dispute Commissions.

title: Representation of the People Act, 1951
description: Act No. 43 of 1951. Provides for the conduct of elections of the Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures, qualifications, and disqualifications.

title: The Interest Act, 1978
description: Act No. 14 of 1978. Regulates the allowance of interest in certain cases in civil proceedings.

title: The Limitation Act, 1963
ministry: Ministry of Law and Justice
longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the law for the limitation of suits and other proceedings and for purposes connected therewith.
description: Act No. 36 of 1963. Governs periods of limitation for instituting suits, appeals, and applications in Indian courts, exclusion of time in legal proceedings, and condonation of delay.
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.content:
(1) This Act may be called the Limitation Act, 1963.
(2) It extends to the whole of India.

sections.title: Bar of limitation
sections.content: (1) Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 24 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence.

sections.title: Extension of prescribed period in certain cases (Condonation of Delay)
sections.content: Any appeal or any application, other than an application under any of the provisions of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, may be admitted after the prescribed period, if the appellant or the applicant satisfies the court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period.

title: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
ministry: Ministry of Law and Justice
longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to domestic arbitration, international commercial arbitration and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards.
description: Act No. 26 of 1996. Consolidated statutory framework for domestic arbitration, conciliation, international commercial arbitration, and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards.
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

sections.title: Arbitration agreement
sections.content: (1) In this Part, 'arbitration agreement' means an agreement by the parties to submit to arbitration all or certain disputes which have arisen or which may arise between them in respect of a defined legal relationship, whether contractual or not.

sections.title: Interim measures, etc., by Court
sections.content: A party may, before or during arbitral proceedings or at any time after the making of the arbitral award but before it is enforced in accordance with section 36, apply to a court for interim measures of protection.

sections.title: Appointment of arbitrators
sections.content: A person of any nationality may be an arbitrator, unless otherwise agreed by the parties. Court shall appoint arbitrator where party fails to agree.

title: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
ministry: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to motor vehicles.
description: Act No. 59 of 1988. Regulates licensing of drivers, vehicle registration, traffic rules, insurance of motor vehicles against third party risks, and Motor Accident Claims Tribunals (MACT).
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

chapters.title: Insurance of Motor Vehicles Against Third Party Risks

sections.title: Application for compensation
sections.content: (1) An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of section 165 may be made— (a) by the person who has sustained the injury; or (b) by the owner of the property; or (c) where death has resulted from the accident, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased.

title: The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
ministry: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Law and Justice
longTitle: An Act to define and amend the law relating to Promissory Notes, Bills of Exchange and Cheques.
description: Act No. 26 of 1881. Governs promissory notes, bills of exchange, cheques, dishonour of cheques for insufficiency of funds (Section 138), statutory demand notice, and interim compensation (Section 143A).
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

chapters.title: Of Penalties in Case of Dishonour of Certain Cheques for Insufficiency of Funds in the Accounts

sections.title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account
sections.content: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid...

sections.title: Offences by companies
sections.content: (1) If the person committing an offence under section 138 is a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company...

sections.title: Power to direct interim compensation
sections.content: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the Court trying an offence under section 138 may order the drawer of the cheque to pay interim compensation to the complainant.

longTitle: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to reorganisation and insolvency resolution of corporate persons, partnership firms and individuals in a time bound manner.
description: Act No. 31 of 2016. Unified framework governing Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), NCLT proceedings, moratorium under Section 14, operational & financial creditors (Sections 7 & 9), and liquidation.
sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

sections.title: Initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process by financial creditor
sections.content: A financial creditor either by itself or jointly with other financial creditors may file an application for initiating corporate insolvency resolution process against a corporate debtor before the Adjudicating Authority when a default has occurred.

sections.title: Moratorium
sections.content: Subject to provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3), on the insolvency commencement date, the Adjudicating Authority shall by order declare moratorium for prohibiting the institution of suits or continuation of pending suits against the corporate debtor...

sourceAuthority: India Code / Legislative Department, Govt. of India

sections.title: Power of entry, search, seizure and arrest without warrant or authorisation
sections.content: Any such officer (being an officer superior in rank to a peon, sepoy or constable) of the departments of central excise, narcotics, customs, revenue intelligence or any other department of a State Government empowered in this behalf...

sections.title: Conditions under which search of persons shall be conducted
sections.content: When any officer authorised under section 42 is about to search any person under the provisions of section 41, section 42 or section 43, he shall, if such person so requires, take such person without unnecessary delay to the nearest Gazetted Officer of any of the departments mentioned in section 42 or to the nearest Magistrate.
